text:
jess (support): Heads up — Acme (customer) escalated. Their mobile app sees streaming cutoffs mid-response, then reconnects and shows duplicated token billing. They pasted SDK logs below.

jess (support): Logs:```
[2024-02-11T14:05:12.345Z] stream.write failed: errno=11 (EAGAIN)
[2024-02-11T14:05:12.347Z] retrying write (1/3)
[2024-02-11T14:05:12.351Z] stream.abort: reason=socket_unwritable
[2024-02-11T14:05:12.352Z] client reconnect: new stream id=abc123
[2024-02-11T14:05:12.360Z] billing: tokens_emitted=67, invoice_event_id=evt_987
```

chris (sre): Thanks. Can you grab the server-side trace for that timeframe (proxy / sidecar logs and runtime logs)? Also run `ss -tanp` and `cat /proc/net/sockstat` on the host if possible. Suspect sndbuf saturation due to slow consumer.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2024-042 (priority: P2) — assigned to chris and maria.

maria (eng-runtime): Quick theory: when send() returns EAGAIN we currently retry a few times then close the connection to avoid blocking the worker thread. If the client is reading very slowly (mobile background/poor network) the kernel send queue fills and we hit that path. Closing triggers client reconnect which restarts the generation and causes double billing.

maria (eng-runtime): Repro I used locally: start our SSE test server then on client do `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms rate 64kbit` then `curl --no-buffer` — stream stalls, server write spikes and eventually our abort path triggers.

chris (sre): Can you paste the sidecar write errors from runtime? Also please include `ss -ti state established | grep <client-ip>` to show `rto`, `rx_queue`, `tx_queue`.

jess (support): Customer provided a small pcap excerpt, here's the sidecar snippet they sent:```
[sidecar] WARN send_chunk: writev failed -> EAGAIN (fd=72)
[sidecar] INFO send_chunk: retrying nonblocking
[sidecar] WARN output_flush: reached retry_limit -> abort_stream
[sidecar] INFO stream_closed: reason=client_unwritable; request_id=abc123
```

chris (sre): That matches. Two immediate mitigations: 1) increase SO_SNDBUF for eventstream connections (gives more kernel queue headroom), 2) switch abort path to exponential backoff + drop partial frames policy (so we don't abort as quickly). Both temporary.

maria (eng-runtime): Long term fixes: a) track emission ack state before billing — bill only when chunk confirmed sent OR when request completes successfully (or implement request-id dedupe on billing events). b) make write path resilient: if write returns EAGAIN, push payload into an internal per-connection bounded queue and continue serving other coroutines; only drop when queue overflows. c) surface per-request client_readiness metrics to console + alerting.

billing-team: We should not double-bill on reconnects. If runtime cannot guarantee idempotent billing, we must switch to billing on final ack. Need eng + billing design call.

chris (sre): Diagnostic commands for ops to run against the host (copy/paste to customer if they'd like):```
# live TCP stats for connections to customer IP
ss -ti dst 198.51.100.23
# kernel socket usage
cat /proc/net/sockstat
# per-socket kernel info (replace FD)
sudo awk '/72:/,/^$/' /proc/net/tcp
# quick trace of EAGAIN events in sidecar logs
grep -n "EAGAIN" /var/log/sidecar.log | tail -50
```

jess (support): Customer tried bumping keepalive and it reduced frequency but didn't eliminate. They are on flaky cellular network and their SDK read loop parks when the app goes background for a few seconds.

maria (eng-runtime): For immediate customer workaround: set the SDK to auto-reconnect with exponential backoff and `idempotency_key` on the generation request so duplicated reconnects won't be billed twice. Also enable client-side windowing (so mobile reads partial frames more aggressively).

chris (sre): We also need to check our sidecar socket options. Proposal: `setsockopt(SO_SNDBUF, 1MB)` for streaming clients, and increase internal retry_limit from 3 -> 8 with backoff 50ms->200ms. I'll prepare a small sidecar patch.

maria (eng-runtime): Repro snippet (for eng):```python
# tiny repro server that writes fast and triggers EAGAIN when client is slow
import socket, time, sys
s = socket.socket()
s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 9001))
s.listen(1)
conn, _ = s.accept()
conn.setblocking(False)
for i in range(1000):
    try:
        conn.send(b\"data-chunk-%d\\n\" % i)
    except BlockingIOError:
        # simulate our old behavior: abort after some retries
        print('EAGAIN at', i)
        break
    time.sleep(0.001)
```

alex (customer-success): I told Acme we'll provide a mitigation plan plus an ETA. They want credits if we can't prevent duplicates.

billing-team: Put a hold on auto-invoicing for the affected window until we confirm dedupe. We'll coordinate credits if needed.

maria (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) chris to roll sidecar SO_SNDBUF bump and retry-tuning to canary (today). 2) maria to spec internal queue + billing idempotency change (design doc by EOD). 3) support (jess) to deliver workaround steps to customer + request pcap/host outputs. 4) billing to pause auto-invoice for incident window.

chris (sre): Rolling canary now to region-us-east-1. I'll watch for increased memory/queue usage. Will post rollout status in this thread.

jess (support): Thanks — customer on call at 16:00 UTC, please have someone from eng/billing join.

oncall-bot: Rollout started: sidecar-config v2.3.1-canary -> us-east-1 (deployment id: dpl_5421).

chris (sre): Canary looks good so far (no crash, sidecar memory up ~2%). Observed fewer abort_stream logs in the canary hosts for the last 30m.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll follow up with a short RFC for billing idempotency + a patch to queue writes for streaming connections. Expect PR tomorrow.

jess (support): Customer call: Acme agreed to temporary SDK changes and wants a postmortem + credit plan. Scheduling follow-up after eng/billing sync.

billing-team: Noted. We'll prepare a provisional credit amount and finalize after dedupe validation.

chris (sre): Closing loop here; keep this thread for rollout/PM notes. If anyone has a new log snippet drop it in and tag me. :thumbsup:
